title: Praise the Lord, When Blushing Morning
description: Praise the Lord, When Blushing Morning in Tonic Solfa to GALILEE (JUDE), doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 393, “Hymn of Spring”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GALILEE (JUDE); any other Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise the Lord, when blush-ing morn-ing Wakes the blos-soms fresh with dew! When the world, a-gain cre-a-ted, Beams with beau-ties fair and new!

lines: Praise the Lord, when blushing morning
Wakes the blossoms fresh with dew!
Beams with beauties fair and new!
Praise the Lord, when early breezes
Come so fragrant from the flowers!
Praise, thou willow by the brookside!
Praise, ye birds, among the bowers!
Praise the Lord! and may His blessing
Guide us in the way of truth,
Keep our feet from paths of error,
Make us holy in our youth.
Praise the Lord, ye hosts of heaven!
All things utter forth His glory!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to GALILEE (JUDE) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
